definitions.explanation: Negotiating or making a request directly with the person in charge, bypassing intermediaries or formal channels. Implies boldness or determination.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}に{直談判|じかだんぱん}した。
examples.english: I went directly to the company president to negotiate.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}を{通|とお}さず、{部長|ぶちょう}に{直談判|じかだんぱん}するのは{勇気|ゆうき}がいる。
examples.english: It takes courage to go directly to the department head without going through your boss.

examples.japanese: {家賃|やちん}の{値下|ねさ}げを{求|もと}めて、{大家|おおや}さんに{直談判|じかだんぱん}しに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to negotiate directly with the landlord to ask for a rent reduction.

notes:
USAGE:
The {直|じか} here is the same as in {直|じか}に (directly, in person). This word carries a nuance of bypassing the usual process and going straight to someone with authority or responsibility. It can suggest boldness, resolve, or even slight impropriety depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～に{直談判|じかだんぱん}する: to negotiate directly with ~
- {直談判|じかだんぱん}しに{行|い}く: to go and negotiate in person
- {社長|しゃちょう}に{直談判|じかだんぱん}: to go directly to the president
- {思|おも}い{切|き}って{直談判|じかだんぱん}する: to take the plunge and negotiate directly
